claims.text: Bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen has oxygen present as lattice defects.
Oxygen defects distort the local lattice structure in bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
Sampling multiple oxygen-defect configurations captures local lattice distortions and scattering centers.
The 0–200 K conductivity regime is quantum dominated.
The 300–1200 K conductivity regime is thermally activated.
Oxygen-defect ensembles alter bond lengths and chemical order in HfNbTaTiZr.
Oxygen-induced structural changes modify phonon dispersions and electronic states.
Between 0 and 200 K, quantum effects and oxygen-defect-induced localized states govern conductivity.
Between 300 and 1200 K, oxygen-defect migration and phonon-electron interactions dominate conductivity.
Explicit ensemble sampling of oxygen defects predicts conductivity more accurately than models based on ideal, defect-free crystals.
The proposed framework can predict effective electronic and thermal conductivity within ±10% of experimental measurements.
The experimental electrical conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen at 500 K is approximately 200 S/m.
Analytical predictions based on defect-free crystals have limited predictive accuracy because they omit experimentally relevant oxygen-induced defects.
The proposed approach is directly applicable to bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen over 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
Application to other compositions or temperature regimes requires additional validation.

contradictions.description: The predicted accuracy target is ±10%, but the hypothesis is only falsified when error exceeds ±20%. Results with errors between 10% and 20% would violate the stated predicted outcome without satisfying the stated falsification rule.
